title: Proverbs 3:5 (KJV)
paragraphs:
Proverbs 3:5 (KJV)
“Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.”
The war between control and surrender.

God is not asking for a little trust.
Not a backup-plan trust.
Not a “Lord, I’ll trust You after I figure it out” kind of trust.

That means when the door stays closed.
When the answer delays.
When the pain makes no sense.
When your own wisdom is too weak to carry the weight.

And this verse is not calling you to stop thinking.
It is calling you to stop treating your understanding like it is your savior.

Jesus is your Savior.
Not your logic.
Not your plans.
Not your ability to predict tomorrow.

Trusting the Lord means placing your whole life in His hands and believing that His wisdom is better than your sight. And at the center of that trust is Christ—who went to the cross, rose again, and proved that even when everything looks lost, God is still writing redemption.

Release the wheel.
Lay down the fear.
And trust the One who never fails.

Prayer:
Lord, teach me to trust You with all my heart. When I cannot understand what You are doing, help me rest in who You are. I surrender my plans, my fears, and my future to You. In Jesus’ name, amen.
